service_boundary: Represents Fireworks-hosted model APIs and deployments, not model publishers, Fireworks client libraries, or customer-operated inference runtimes.
regional_controls: Regional and private deployment options are enterprise- and deployment-specific; public serverless placement is not universally customer-selected.
retention_controls: Data handling follows Fireworks terms and feature-specific behavior for serverless inference, batch files, fine-tunes, and deployments.
routing: Customers select a model or deployment; Fireworks manages serving capacity rather than routing to unrelated upstream providers.
customization: Fine-tuning, LoRA, custom models, and dedicated deployments are documented for supported formats.
strengths: Multiple capacity modes support both bursty and predictable workloads.
OpenAI-compatible APIs cover a broad hosted model catalog.
tradeoffs: Production controls depend on deployment tier and contract.
Publisher terms and model lifecycle remain model-specific.

response_integrity.note: No signature, attestation, or equivalent mechanism for verifying that a response arrived unaltered from the model appears in the API reference or the security documentation.
response_integrity.scope: Fireworks data-security guide, for Fireworks AI

upstream_disclosure.note: The public trust centre names the third party that receives content for select models, in an update published 2026-03-23: "Fireworks AI uses Anthropic PBC as a Sub-processor to power select AI services. We have entered into a zero data retention agreement with Anthropic, under which no User Content or Output is retained by Anthropic following the completion of a request." The data-security guide states Fireworks does not log or store prompts for open models without opt-in.
upstream_disclosure.scope: Fireworks trust centre subprocessor updates, for Fireworks AI

credential_handling.note: The API offers no customer-supplied-key path: keys are created by the Fireworks API-key endpoint, whose reference even records whether "the plaintext value of the API key is unknown to Fireworks", and every documented request uses a Fireworks key.
credential_handling.scope: Fireworks create-API-key reference, for Fireworks AI

cache_isolation.note: The prompt-caching guide states: "Serverless deployments maintain separate caches for each Fireworks account to prevent data leakage and timing attacks." The same guide describes on-demand deployments as a customer's own capacity.
cache_isolation.scope: Fireworks prompt-caching guide, for Fireworks AI

vulnerability_disclosure.note: The public trust centre publishes a security contact, security@fireworks.ai, and a vulnerability disclosure portal; the data-security guide itself names no contact.
vulnerability_disclosure.scope: Fireworks trust centre, for Fireworks AI

independent_audit.note: The platform's own security-and-compliance guide states "SOC 2 Type II (certified)" and lists ISO 27001 as achieved; the public trust centre lists SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001:2022, ISO 27701, and ISO/IEC 42001 with reports behind a request-access control. The guide names no product scope beyond the platform it documents.
independent_audit.scope: Fireworks data-security guide, for Fireworks AI

findings.claim: In 7 of these providers, we detected global cache sharing. The audit table records caching detected at the global level for Fireworks AI's Llama 3.1 8B Instruct endpoint; the audits were conducted in September and early October 2024 and disclosed to each provider in October 2024.

source.label: Auditing Prompt Caching in Language Model APIs, arXiv 2502.07776v2

resolved.summary: The current prompt-caching guide states that serverless deployments maintain separate caches for each Fireworks account; the paper does not name Fireworks among the providers that confirmed a change.
